chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Muʿādh ibn Muslim, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Whenever any doubt enters upon you in your salat (prayer), then act upon the greater number; then when you have finished, complete what you thought you had omitted. And it is possible that the report is specific to the nawāfil, for the more excellent practice in the nawāfil is to build upon the lesser number, as we have explained.

key_terms.الشَّكِّ: doubt arising during the performance of salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْأَكْثَرِ: the greater number, which one is instructed to rely upon in the doubt
key_terms.الْبِنَاءُ عَلَى الْأَقَلِّ: proceeding on the basis of the lesser number in counting
key_terms.انْصَرَفْتَ: you finished and departed from the salat (prayer)
key_terms.صَلَاتِكَ: your salat (prayer), the act of ritual worship being discussed
key_terms.نَقَصْتَ: you omitted or fell short of something in the salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if doubt occurs during salat (prayer) about the number of rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for doubt during salat (prayer), instructing one to proceed on the basis of the greater number and then make up what one thinks may have been omitted after finishing. It also notes a possible specification regarding nawāfil, where building upon the lesser number is considered preferable.
